theorem one_guard_closes_both_leaks [DecidableEq A] (L : Ledger A) (s d : A)
    (hs : s ∈ L.live) (hd : d ∈ L.live) (v : ℕ) :
    ((Accounting.ofSetBalSub L s v hs).burn = v ↔ v ≤ L.bal s)
      ∧ (((L.setBal s (L.bal s - v) hs).setBal d
            ((L.setBal s (L.bal s - v) hs).bal d + v) hd).supply = L.supply
          ↔ v ≤ L.bal s) :=
  ⟨reported_burn_eq_request_iff L s v hs,
   Ledger.xfer_supply_neutral_iff L s d v hs hd⟩
properties.x_fidelity_reason: Packet imports revert/rejection semantics the theorem does not model (FACT-2/FACT-3 expected, OBS-1), and OBS-2 inverts FACT-2 by flagging any burn computed as min(v, bal(s)) — the Lean evidence defines Accounting.ofSetBalSub.burn as exactly min(v, bal(s)), with burn = v holding precisely under v <= bal(s).

audit_packet.guarantee: A single condition v <= bal(s), compared against the source balance of the pre-update ledger, is exactly equivalent to BOTH (a) the recorded burn equalling the requested amount v and (b) total supply being unchanged across the paired debit/credit. Both equivalences are two-directional, and when the condition fails both quantities are off by exactly v - bal(s).
preconditions: Hypothesis hs: the source account s is a member of the live account list (s in L.live) of the ledger the debit is applied to.
Hypothesis hd: the destination account d is a member of the live account list of the ledger that already reflects the debit.
The live account list is duplicate-free (Ledger.live_distinct / Distinct L.live); supply is defined as sumOver bal over exactly that list.
Balances are naturals, so subtraction saturates at 0 instead of going negative.

supporting_facts.claim: One condition governs two properties: burn accuracy holds if and only if v <= bal(s), and supply preservation holds if and only if v <= bal(s). Both are iff, not one-way implications.
supporting_facts.check: Identify the condition that admits a balance-decreasing update, and confirm a single condition equivalent to v <= bal(s) governs both the recorded burn amount and the balance update.
supporting_facts.expected: One condition, evaluated against the source balance of the state the update is applied to, decides both outcomes; when it holds both properties hold, and when it is absent both are violable.
supporting_facts.flag_if: No such condition exists, it governs only the recorded accounting while the balance update proceeds, it governs only the balance update while the burn is computed independently, or it is compared against a source balance other than the one the debit is applied to.

supporting_facts.claim: The recorded burn is exactly min(v, bal(s)): it never exceeds bal(s) (L003), and it equals the requested v exactly when v <= bal(s) (L004). Keep the exact equality burn = min(v, bal(s)); do not weaken it to 'burn is nonzero' or 'the debit succeeded'.
supporting_facts.check: Compare the burn amount the implementation records against the requested amount v, both when v <= bal(s) and when the source is under-funded (v > bal(s)).
supporting_facts.expected: With v <= bal(s): recorded burn == v exactly, since min(v, bal(s)) = v. With v > bal(s): the recorded burn is bal(s), short of v by exactly v - bal(s).
supporting_facts.flag_if: A burn exceeding bal(s) is recorded, or a clamped burn of bal(s) is consumed downstream as if it were the requested v on a path where v > bal(s) — an under-report of exactly v - bal(s).

supporting_facts.claim: Quantified failure: an unguarded debit-then-credit gives supply' = supply + (v - bal(s)) (L007, from L011 with the identity L013). The shortfall is not merely 'supply may change' — it is exactly the amount by which the source was overdrawn.
supporting_facts.check: With v > bal(s), sum bal over all live accounts before and after the paired debit/credit and take the difference.
supporting_facts.expected: No applied debit-then-credit has v > bal(s); every applied pair satisfies the condition, so this difference is never exercised.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A debit-then-credit is applied with v > bal(s): post-state supply exceeds pre-state supply by exactly v - bal(s); equivalently the source saturates to 0 while the destination is credited the full v.

supporting_facts.claim: Conservation is exact and two-directional: with v <= bal(s) post-transfer supply equals pre-transfer supply exactly (L008); and supply' = supply forces v <= bal(s) (L005/L009/L014, since v - bal(s) = 0 iff v <= bal(s)). Keep the exact equality, not 'supply is approximately preserved'.
supporting_facts.check: For an accepted transfer with v <= bal(s), compare the total over all live accounts before and after, including the boundary cases v = 0, v = bal(s), and s = d.
supporting_facts.expected: supply_after == supply_before exactly for every accepted transfer.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any accepted transfer changes the total, or a supply-equality check is used as the only safety net in place of the v <= bal(s) condition.

supporting_facts.claim: Per-write accounting: crediting d raises supply by exactly v (L015), debiting s lowers it by exactly min(v, bal(s)) (L016), and any single-account write shifts supply by exactly the difference between the new and old value (L020, L021). Each write carries a membership hypothesis on the account written.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm each balance write targets an account established as a member of the live list, and that no extra or duplicate write is issued for the same account within the operation.
supporting_facts.expected: Exactly one debit write for s and one credit write for d, each on a live account, with d's new value computed from its balance in the post-debit state.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A write targets an account not established as live, the destination credit is computed from a pre-debit balance of d (mis-handling s == d), or an additional write shifts supply outside the two accounted amounts.

supporting_facts.claim: The supply summation is only well-behaved when the account list is duplicate-free and the updated account is a member: updating a non-member leaves the sum unchanged (L024), so a balance written for an unlisted account is invisible to the supply total (L022 gives the member case).
supporting_facts.check: Verify the enumerated account list admits no duplicate entries and that both s and d resolve to entries of the same list used to compute the total supply.
supporting_facts.expected: Accounts are uniquely keyed; membership of s and d in the live list is established for their respective writes.
supporting_facts.flag_if: An account can appear twice in the enumerated list, or a balance can be written for an account absent from the list the supply total is summed over — either breaks conservation independently of the v <= bal(s) condition.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm the condition v <= bal(s) is decided against the source balance of the state the debit is applied to, and that no debit-then-credit is applied on a path where it fails.
derived_obligations.expected: Every applied debit-then-credit satisfies v <= bal(s), decided on the pre-debit source balance of s.
derived_obligations.flag_if: No such condition exists, saturating subtraction is relied on in its place (leaving burn = min(v, bal(s)) and supply' = supply + (v - bal(s))), or it is decided against a source balance that already reflects the debit.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm the recorded burn equals the amount actually removed from s, i.e. min(v, bal(s)), and that any consumer treating the burn as the requested v is reachable only where v <= bal(s).
derived_obligations.expected: burn == min(v, bal(s)) on every path; burn == v exactly on the paths satisfying the condition, where the two coincide.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A burn larger than the amount actually removed (> bal(s)) is recorded, or a clamped burn of bal(s) is consumed as the requested amount v on a path not covered by the condition.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm both membership hypotheses are discharged: s is a member of the live list for the debit, and d is a member for the credit against the post-debit state.
derived_obligations.expected: Both accounts resolved as members of the live list for their respective writes.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Either account is written without establishing membership, or d's membership is established only against the pre-debit state.

derived_obligations.check: Sum bal over all live accounts before and after an accepted transfer, covering v = 0, v = bal(s), and s = d.
derived_obligations.expected: Totals are exactly equal in every accepted case.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any accepted transfer changes the total, most notably the s = d case where the credit uses a pre-debit destination balance.

audit_packet.derivation: ROOT is the conjunction of L001 and L002. L001 unfolds Accounting.ofSetBalSub, whose burn field is min(v, bal(s)); L003 gives min(v, bal(s)) <= bal(s) always and L004 gives min(v, bal(s)) = v exactly when v <= bal(s), so 'recorded burn == requested v' is equivalent to the bound. L002 comes from the general supply accounting: L020/L021 (with L022/L024 supplying the duplicate-free summation lemma) show a single write shifts supply by exactly the delta; specialising gives L015 (credit raises supply by v) and L016 (debit lowers it by min(v, bal(s))). Composing them yields L011 and, with the identity L013, the shortfall equation L007: supply' = supply + (v - bal(s)). Natural subtraction gives v - bal(s) = 0 exactly when v <= bal(s) (L014 forward; L005/L009 backward), so supply' = supply is likewise equivalent to the bound (L008 for the guarded direction). Both halves hinge on the same condition, and its absence under-reports the burn and raises supply by the same v - bal(s).

omitted_facts.reason: Pure arithmetic: left cancellation of natural addition, used to rearrange the supply equations. No implementation-visible obligation.
Pure arithmetic: right cancellation of natural addition, likewise only equational rearrangement. No implementation-visible obligation.
Commutativity of min — bookkeeping; the security-relevant content (burn = min(v, bal(s)) and burn <= bal(s)) is preserved in FACT-2.
Greatest-lower-bound property of min, used only to establish min_comm. No independent implementation content.
Generic bound min(a,b) <= a used inside min_comm; the operative bound min(v, bal(s)) <= bal(s) is carried as L003 in FACT-2.
Symmetric counterpart of min_eq_left (L004), already carried in FACT-2; adds no distinct obligation.
List eliminator: nothing is a member of the empty list. Base case of the summation induction.
List eliminator for cons-membership; internal induction machinery for the summation lemma. The resulting requirement (membership plus distinctness) is carried in FACT-6.

properties.x_fidelity_reason: The assertion infers "bal unbounded" from failure of the per-step identity; the theorem only establishes the bound W <= supply(0)+sumOver(ms, range n) when the identity holds, and never shows that violating it makes balances unbounded. Rewritten to check the identity and assert the theorem's actual bound.

audit_packet.guarantee: No account balance can attain a threshold W unless the initial supply plus all issuance accounted over the transition window already reaches W. Equivalently, a balance can only grow to a magnitude that accounted minting already justifies. This holds only while every transition maintains the per-step accounting identity supply(i+1) + burned(i) = supply(i) + minted(i); a balance write that bypasses that identity voids the guarantee entirely. W is an arbitrary threshold in the model — the theorem fixes no representation width, wrap point, or numeric constant.
preconditions: ROOT obligation [5] (h): for EVERY transition index i, the accounting identity supply(i+1) + burned(i) = supply(i) + minted(i) holds — no transition may change balances outside this identity, including transitions that touch a single account.

ROOT obligation [9] (hin): the inspected state index i lies at or before the horizon n over which issuance is summed (i <= n) — the balance being bounded must come from a state inside the accounted window.

Model parameter (hover, obligation [11]): W is any threshold attained by the account balance at state i (W <= bal_i(a)). This is a caller-supplied quantity, not an implementation obligation; the theorem attaches no meaning to any particular value of W.

Ledger well-formedness: the live-account list is duplicate-free (Distinct) and every account with a nonzero balance is present in it (bal_live) — otherwise the supply sum omits or double-counts balances and both bounds below collapse.

supporting_facts.claim: For any state index i <= n and any account a, any threshold W attained by that account's balance is also attained by supply(0) + total issuance over the window: W <= bal_i(a) implies W <= supply(0) + sumOver(minted, range n). Reaching any magnitude requires that much accounted issuance.
supporting_facts.check: Pick the threshold of interest and confirm the implementation cannot produce a stored balance at or above it unless supply(0) + summed issuance over the same window also reaches it. Concretely: identify every path that changes an account balance and confirm none raises a balance without either a corresponding accounted issuance term or an equal decrement elsewhere.
supporting_facts.expected: Every balance-increasing write is paired with either an accounted issuance term or an equal decrement elsewhere, so no balance can attain a magnitude exceeding supply(0) + cumulative accounted issuance.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any code path can set or increase a stored balance to a value not covered by supply(0) + accounted issuance — e.g. a write whose increase is never recorded in the accounting term, or an increase applied to one account with no matching decrement or issuance.

supporting_facts.claim: Chain bound (stronger than the final consequence, and stated as an ordering on the balance itself): for i <= n, bal_i(a) <= supply(0) + sumOver(minted, range n). Every single account's balance at every accounted state is bounded by initial supply plus cumulative issuance — not merely 'some mint occurred'.
supporting_facts.check: Assert the ordering directly as a state-consistency check: for the account under audit at any accounted state, its stored balance is <= supply(0) + cumulative accounted issuance up to the window horizon. Exercise it against maximal-balance and long-chain scenarios, not only single-step ones.
supporting_facts.expected: The ordering holds at every accounted state index, for every account, with no dependence on how many transitions have occurred.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A stored balance exceeds supply(0) + cumulative accounted issuance at any accounted state, or the bound is only checked at a single state / a single transition rather than for all i <= n.

supporting_facts.claim: Per-state containment: for any single ledger state L and account a, bal(a) <= supply(L), because a is a member of the duplicate-free live list and a summand never exceeds its sum. This is a bound, not a nonzero property: one account can never hold more than the whole supply of its own state.
supporting_facts.check: Verify that the total-supply quantity is computed as the sum of the balances of a duplicate-free live-account list, and that every account carrying a nonzero balance appears in that list. Then assert bal(a) <= supply for each account of the state under audit.
supporting_facts.expected: Every account balance is <= the state's total supply; the live list contains no duplicates and omits no nonzero-balance account.
supporting_facts.flag_if: An account's balance exceeds its state's total supply; the accounted set can contain the same account twice (double counting inflates supply and hides an over-large balance); or a nonzero balance can exist for an account absent from the accounted set (undercounted supply, silently unbounded balance).

supporting_facts.claim: Exact accumulated conservation (equality, not an inequality): supply(n) + sumOver(burned, range n) = supply(0) + sumOver(minted, range n). Over any window, total supply plus everything burned equals the starting supply plus everything minted.
supporting_facts.check: Independently recompute both sides over a window of transitions and compare for exact equality, using the recomputed supply (sum over live balances) rather than a cached or incrementally-maintained counter.
supporting_facts.expected: Exact equality of the two sides at every window horizon; recomputed supply agrees with any incrementally maintained supply value.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The two sides differ by any amount, or the equality is only enforced as an inequality / only approximately; or a balance write updates an account without updating the corresponding issuance or burn term.

supporting_facts.claim: Monotonicity of the accounted totals: for i <= n, sumOver(f, range i) <= sumOver(f, range n); a per-step nondecreasing quantity satisfies f(i) <= f(n) across the window. A bound established at a later horizon still covers all earlier states.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm the cumulative issuance accumulator never decreases as more transitions are accounted, and that extending the audited window cannot lower the bound used in FACT-1/FACT-2.
supporting_facts.expected: Cumulative issuance is monotonically nondecreasing in the window horizon; per-step issuance terms never subtract from the total.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The cumulative issuance accumulator can decrease when extending the window (a subtraction folded into the mint term), which would make the bound in FACT-1/FACT-2 unsound for earlier states.

derived_obligations.check: Enumerate every code path that changes an account balance and confirm each one is covered by the per-step accounting identity supply(i+1) + burned(i) = supply(i) + minted(i) — i.e. each change either moves value between accounted accounts or is recorded as issuance/burn.
derived_obligations.expected: No balance-changing path exists that is outside the accounting identity; the identity is re-checkable at every transition index i, not just at chosen checkpoints.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any balance-changing path bypasses the accounting identity, or the identity is enforced only for some transition kinds — an unaccounted write is exactly the case the theorem's hypothesis excludes, so no bound is available for it.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm the state whose balances are being bounded is inside the accounted window (i <= n): the issuance total used as the bound must be summed over a horizon reaching at least as far as the state being inspected.
derived_obligations.expected: Every inspected state index is at or before the horizon over which issuance is accumulated; no state's balances are validated against an issuance total that stops earlier.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Balances from a state beyond the accounted horizon are checked against a stale/earlier issuance total, or the window boundary is chosen so that transitions contributing balance increases fall outside the sum.

derived_obligations.check: Verify the account set used to compute total supply is duplicate-free and that no account can hold a nonzero balance while absent from it, across account creation, deletion, and balance-zeroing paths.
derived_obligations.expected: Duplicate-free accounted set; nonzero balance implies membership in it.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Duplicate entries are possible (inflating supply and masking an over-large balance), or an account can retain a nonzero balance after being removed from the accounted set (its value escapes the supply sum entirely).

audit_packet.derivation: The per-state containment bal(a) <= supply (FACT-3, from L002 via the membership bound L005 on the duplicate-free live list) says one account never exceeds its own state's supply. The accumulated conservation equality (FACT-4, L003) rewrites supply(n) + total burned as supply(0) + total minted, and monotonicity of the accumulated sums (FACT-5, L004/L006) lets a bound at horizon n cover every earlier index i <= n. Composing these gives the chain bound bal_i(a) <= supply(0) + total minted over the window (FACT-2, L001). Transitivity with the attained-threshold hypothesis W <= bal_i(a) yields the root conclusion (FACT-1, ROOT): W <= supply(0) + total minted. Read contrapositively, a balance can only attain a magnitude that supply(0) plus accounted issuance already reaches. W is universally quantified over the naturals and the ledger is modelled over unbounded Nat balances, so the theorem states no representation width, wrap behaviour, or numeric constant; the security value rests entirely on root obligation [5] — the bound is proved only under the per-step accounting identity, so if any balance write escapes that identity the theorem supplies no bound at all for the resulting states (it does not, by itself, establish that balances then become unbounded).

omitted_facts.reason: List-structure plumbing (range (n+1) = range n ++ [n]); it decomposes the index range for the inductive step and carries no implementation-observable security condition.

Arithmetic decomposition of a sum over a concatenated list (sumOver (l1 ++ l2) = sumOver l1 + sumOver l2); it is the mechanical basis of the monotonicity fact already reported as FACT-5 and adds no separate check.
Range-restricted variant of the step-monotonicity lemma used only to discharge L006; its security content is fully captured by FACT-5.
Internal accumulator-normalization lemma for the standard range construction (range.loop n acc = range.loop n [] ++ acc); pure library plumbing with no protocol meaning.

audit_packet.guarantee: A destroy step applied to an account a that is a member of the pre-state ledger's live set conserves total supply exactly: supply(post-state) + burned(trace) = supply(pre-state) + minted(trace), where the trace is exactly one burn event of amount bal_before(a) attributed to a and nothing is minted. Any implementation of this step over a duplicate-free live set, using the zero-then-erase order, must therefore compute an identical post-state supply and an identical emitted event trace; deviation means value is destroyed or created without a matching event, or two implementations of the same step disagree on the post-state.
preconditions: Scope hypothesis ha: the statement covers destroy steps whose target a is a member of the pre-state ledger's live set (a in M.live). Destroy steps applied to an account outside the live set are outside this evidence; the checks below are asserted only for in-scope steps.

Ledger structure invariant live_distinct: the live account list is duplicate-free (EthTotal.Distinct M.live). The supply accounting lemmas hold only over a duplicate-free live set, so distinctness is checkable state, not a free assumption.
Ledger structure invariant bal_live: any account with a nonzero balance is a member of the live set (bal a != 0 -> a in live), so no balance sits outside the summed live set.
Balances and supply are non-negative unbounded naturals (Nat): the equalities below must be evaluated without wraparound or saturating arithmetic.

supporting_facts.claim: Exact supply conservation across the destroy step: supply(post-state) + burned(trace) = supply(pre-state) + minted(trace); on the destroy trace this is the exact equality supply_after + bal_before(a) = supply_before with minted = 0. It is an equality, not an inequality or a 'supply does not increase' bound.
supporting_facts.check: Recompute total supply as the sum of balances over all live accounts immediately before and immediately after the destroy step, and take the burned amount from the emitted burn event. Assert supply_after + burned == supply_before and burned == bal_before(a) exactly.
supporting_facts.expected: supply_after + burned == supply_before; burned == bal_before(a); minted == 0.
supporting_facts.flag_if: supply_after + burned != supply_before; or burned differs from the target's pre-destroy balance (partial burn, rounded burn, balance read after zeroing, or a balance read for a different account); or any amount is minted by the step.

supporting_facts.claim: The pre-erase zeroing is an exact read-back equality: after writing balance v to a, reading a's balance through the same accessor returns exactly v; with v = 0 this establishes bal(a) = 0 in the intermediate state. Not merely 'the balance was cleared' or 'is falsy'.
supporting_facts.check: In the intermediate state produced before the erase, read the target's balance back through the same accessor the supply sum uses and compare it to 0.
supporting_facts.expected: bal(a) == 0 in the intermediate state, observed through the accessor used by the supply computation.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The read-back is nonzero, absent/undefined, or served from a different state view than the one the supply sum enumerates.

supporting_facts.claim: Erasing an account from the live set changes total supply by exactly zero, and this holds only under the hypothesis bal(a) = 0. The order is load-bearing: zero the balance, then erase from the live set.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm the implementation writes the target's balance to 0 before removing it from the live set, and that the removal itself is supply-neutral: recompute the supply sum immediately before and immediately after the removal.
supporting_facts.expected: supply(after removal) == supply(before removal), with the removed account's balance already 0 at the moment of removal.
supporting_facts.flag_if: An account is removed from the live set while still holding a nonzero balance (erase-before-zero, or an erase path with no zero guard), which drops value with no matching burn event; or the removal step changes the supply sum.

supporting_facts.claim: Balance-update accounting over the live set is exact: supply(setBal a v) + bal_before(a) = supply_before + v, valid because a occurs in the duplicate-free live set; the same lemma family gives that an update aimed at an account absent from the enumerated list leaves that list's sum unchanged.
supporting_facts.check: For the destroy's zeroing write (v = 0), assert supply(after zeroing) + bal_before(a) == supply_before. Independently assert the enumerated live set holds no duplicate entry for the target.
supporting_facts.expected: supply(after zeroing) + bal_before(a) == supply_before; the target occurs at most once in the live set.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The equality fails; or the target appears more than once in the enumerated live set, so its balance is double-counted in supply or only one copy is erased.

supporting_facts.claim: Burn-site confinement: every event in the emitted trace that carries a burn site has that site equal to the destroyed account a — the burn set is the singleton {a}. Value may be debited only from the account being destroyed.
supporting_facts.check: Inspect the events emitted by the destroy step and assert every event carrying a burn site names exactly a.
supporting_facts.expected: Every burn-site value in the trace equals a; the burn set is exactly {a}.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A burn is attributed to any account other than the destroyed one, or a burn event carries a missing/placeholder site.

supporting_facts.claim: Mint-site confinement against the empty set: the destroy step's mint set is empty, so no emitted event carries a mint site, and minted(trace) = 0.
supporting_facts.check: Assert the destroy step emits zero events carrying a mint site and that the minted total over its trace is 0.
supporting_facts.expected: No mint-site event in the trace; minted == 0.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any event carrying a mint site is emitted by the destroy step, or minted != 0.

supporting_facts.claim: The trace is the exact singleton [burn(a, bal_before(a))]: any event that is a member of the trace is that one burn event, and nothing is a member of an empty trace. Event shape and multiplicity are pinned, not bounded.
supporting_facts.check: Assert the destroy step emits exactly one event, whose kind is burn, whose site is a, and whose amount equals bal_before(a); assert no additional events (duplicate burns, retries, zero-amount fillers) accompany it.
supporting_facts.expected: Emitted event count == 1 and that event == burn(a, bal_before(a)).
supporting_facts.flag_if: Zero events emitted for a destroy that changed supply; more than one event emitted; or the single event's kind, site, or amount deviates from burn(a, bal_before(a)).

derived_obligations.check: Instrument the destroy step with a differential check: snapshot the summed supply over live accounts before and after, and compare against the burned/minted totals derived from the emitted events, using unbounded arithmetic.
derived_obligations.expected: supply_after + burned == supply_before + minted, with minted == 0 and burned == bal_before(a).
derived_obligations.flag_if: The identity fails for any destroy step, or the arithmetic can wrap/saturate so the identity holds only modulo a word size.

derived_obligations.check: Determine, for each destroy path, whether the target's membership in the live set is established before the accounting identity is relied on. Assert the identity on the paths where it is; record paths where membership is not established as outside this evidence rather than asserting a behaviour for them.
derived_obligations.expected: Every path on which the identity is asserted has the target in the live set; paths without established membership are explicitly listed as uncovered.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The conservation identity is claimed for a step whose target was never shown to be in the enumerated live set, or the burned amount is taken from a default balance for an account whose membership is unknown.

derived_obligations.check: Verify the step order in code: the target's balance is written to 0, that zero is observable through the accessor used by the supply computation, and only then is the account removed from the live set.
derived_obligations.expected: Zero-then-erase order on every destroy path, with the removal taken against an observed bal(a) == 0.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any path erases first, or erases with no zero check, or the zeroing write and the erase guard read different state views so the guard sees a stale balance.

derived_obligations.check: Assert the live account set enumerated by the supply computation contains no duplicate entry for the target, before and after the destroy.
derived_obligations.expected: The live set is duplicate-free; the destroyed account occurs zero times after the destroy.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The target appears twice in the live set (balance double-counted in supply, or one copy left live after the erase), or the target is still present in the live set after the destroy.

derived_obligations.check: Compare the emitted event trace against the expected singleton field by field: one burn event, site == destroyed account, amount == pre-destroy balance, zero mint-site events.
derived_obligations.expected: Exactly one event equal to burn(a, bal_before(a)); no mint-site events.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Event count, kind, site, or amount deviates in any way, so two implementations of the same step could emit different traces for identical input state.

derived_obligations.check: Assert the destroy step touches no account other than a: the zeroing write leaves every other account's balance unchanged, and no address other than a enters or leaves the live set.
derived_obligations.expected: Only the target's balance and its live-set membership change.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any other account's balance changes, or any other address enters/leaves the live set during the destroy step.

audit_packet.derivation: The root theorem is a pair over an abstract ledger (live list + balance function), with no client, opcode, or transaction-format content — so all checks are phrased over the ledger step itself. The supply conjunct is acc_destroy (L002), i.e. supply_destroy (L005) with burned/minted evaluated on the singleton trace (burned([burn a v]) = v, minted([burn a v]) = 0). supply_destroy composes three exact equalities: the destroy guard (L001, from setBal_bal_self L004 / setBalOfPoint_bal_self L009) giving read-back of exactly 0 after zeroing; supply_eraseLive (L010, from sumOver_eraseOne_of_zero L013 / L017) giving that erasing a zero-balance account leaves the sum unchanged — which is why zero-then-erase order is load-bearing; and supply_setBal_zero (L011, the v = 0 case of supply_setBal L014, from sumOver_update L018 / L019, which needs the live list duplicate-free and containing the target, with L020 covering the not-in-list case). The confinement conjunct is SiteConfined.burn (L003): forall_mem_singleton (L006, via eqOfMemSingleton L012, memConsElim L015, notMemNil L016) reduces the obligation to the one emitted event; no_site (L007) discharges the mint side vacuously since a burn event has no mint site, giving the empty mint set; site_singleton (L008) pins the burn side to {a}. The hypothesis ha is the statement's scope, not a proved rejection behaviour, so OBS-2 asserts coverage and records uncovered paths instead of demanding a reject-or-no-op. Weakening any equality to a bound — supply merely not increasing, the balance merely 'cleared' rather than exactly 0, or 'a burn was emitted' rather than exactly one burn of the exact pre-destroy amount at site a — would admit a post-state and event trace this evidence does not pin, with fund-integrity impact.

properties.text: Verify the fee-escrow settlement: each escrow payout amount is <= the escrow balance at that step, the escrow ends at its pre-settlement balance, cumulative burned rises by exactly B with minted unchanged (and zero), supply <= initial, live set unchanged.
properties.assertion: R+(T+B)=P & P<=bal0(sender) & escrow!=sender,coinbase & bal'(escrow)=bal0(escrow) & burned'=burned+B & minted'=minted=0 & supply'+burned'=supply0 & live'=live2
properties.label: gas
properties.lean_statement:
∀ {A : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq A] (L₀ : EthTotal.Ledger A) (sender escrow coinbase : A),
  Ne escrow sender →
    Ne escrow coinbase →
      ∀ (hs₀ : List.instMembership.mem L₀.live sender) (he₀ : List.instMembership.mem L₀.live escrow) (P R T B : Nat),
        Eq (instHAdd.hAdd R (instHAdd.hAdd T B)) P →
          instLENat.le P (L₀.bal sender) →
            ∀ (L₂ : EthTotal.Ledger A) (τe : EthTotal.Trace A),
              List.instMembership.mem L₂.live sender →
                List.instMembership.mem L₂.live escrow →
                  List.instMembership.mem L₂.live coinbase →
                    Eq (L₂.bal escrow) (instHAdd.hAdd (L₀.bal escrow) P) →
                      Eq (instHAdd.hAdd L₂.supply (EthTotal.burned τe))
                          (instHAdd.hAdd
                            ((L₀.setBal sender (instHSub.hSub (L₀.bal sender) P) hs₀).setBal escrow
                                (instHAdd.hAdd ((L₀.setBal sender (instHSub.hSub (L₀.bal sender) P) hs₀).bal escrow) P)
                                he₀).supply
                            (EthTotal.minted τe)) →
                        EthTotal.SiteConfined List.nil (List.cons escrow List.nil) τe →
                          Exists fun L' =>
                            Exists fun τ =>
                              And
                                (Eq τ (instHAppendOfAppend.hAppend τe (List.cons (EthTotal.Ev.burn escrow B) List.nil)))
                                (And
                                  (Eq (instHAdd.hAdd L'.supply (EthTotal.burned τ))
                                    (instHAdd.hAdd L₀.supply (EthTotal.minted τ)))
                                  (And (Eq (EthTotal.burned τ) (instHAdd.hAdd (EthTotal.burned τe) B))
                                    (And (Eq (EthTotal.minted τ) (EthTotal.minted τe))
                                      (And (EthTotal.SiteConfined List.nil (List.cons escrow List.nil) τ)
                                        (And (instLENat.le L'.supply L₀.supply)
                                          (And (Eq (L'.bal escrow) (L₀.bal escrow)) (Eq L'.live L₂.live)))))))

theorem process_transaction_effect [DecidableEq A]
    (L₀ : Ledger A) (sender escrow coinbase : A)
    (hse : escrow ≠ sender) (hec : escrow ≠ coinbase)
    (hs₀ : sender ∈ L₀.live) (he₀ : escrow ∈ L₀.live)
    (P R T B : ℕ) (hsplit : R + (T + B) = P) (hP : P ≤ L₀.bal sender)
    (L₂ : Ledger A) (τe : Trace A)
    (hs₂ : sender ∈ L₂.live) (he₂ : escrow ∈ L₂.live) (hc₂ : coinbase ∈ L₂.live)
    (hesc : L₂.bal escrow = L₀.bal escrow + P)
    (hacce : L₂.supply + burned τe
      = ((L₀.setBal sender (L₀.bal sender - P) hs₀).setBal escrow
          ((L₀.setBal sender (L₀.bal sender - P) hs₀).bal escrow + P) he₀).supply
        + minted τe)
    (hconfe : SiteConfined ([] : List A) [escrow] τe) :
    ∃ (L' : Ledger A) (τ : Trace A),
      τ = τe ++ [Ev.burn escrow B]
      ∧ L'.supply + burned τ = L₀.supply + minted τ
      ∧ burned τ = burned τe + B
      ∧ minted τ = minted τe
      ∧ SiteConfined ([] : List A) [escrow] τ
      ∧ L'.supply ≤ L₀.supply
      ∧ L'.bal escrow = L₀.bal escrow
      ∧ L'.live = L₂.live :=
  let e₀ := L₀.bal escrow
  let L₃ := (L₂.setBal escrow (L₂.bal escrow - R) he₂).setBal sender
    ((L₂.setBal escrow (L₂.bal escrow - R) he₂).bal sender + R) hs₂
  let L₄ := (L₃.setBal escrow (L₃.bal escrow - T) he₂).setBal coinbase
    ((L₃.setBal escrow (L₃.bal escrow - T) he₂).bal coinbase + T) hc₂
  let L₅ := L₄.setBal escrow (L₄.bal escrow - B) he₂
  let hR₂ : R ≤ L₂.bal escrow :=
    Eq.subst (motive := fun n => R ≤ n)
      (Eq.trans (congrArg (fun n => e₀ + n) hsplit) hesc.symm)
      (escrow_guard e₀ R (T + B))
  let e₃ : L₃.bal escrow = e₀ + (T + B) :=
    Eq.trans (Ledger.xfer_bal_src L₂ escrow sender R he₂ hs₂ hse)
      (Eq.trans (congrArg (fun n => n - R) hesc)
        (Eq.trans (congrArg (fun n => (e₀ + n) - R) hsplit.symm)
          (escrow_after e₀ R (T + B))))
  let hT₃ : T ≤ L₃.bal escrow :=
    Eq.subst (motive := fun n => T ≤ n) e₃.symm (escrow_guard e₀ T B)
  let e₄ : L₄.bal escrow = e₀ + B :=
    Eq.trans (Ledger.xfer_bal_src L₃ escrow coinbase T he₂ hc₂ hec)
      (Eq.trans (congrArg (fun n => n - T) e₃) (escrow_after e₀ T B))
  let hB₄ : B ≤ L₄.bal escrow :=
    Eq.subst (motive := fun n => B ≤ n) e₄.symm (escrow_guard e₀ B 0)
  let e₅ : L₅.bal escrow = e₀ :=
    Eq.trans (Ledger.setBal_bal_self L₄ escrow (L₄.bal escrow - B) he₂)
      (Eq.trans (congrArg (fun n => n - B) e₄) (escrow_after e₀ B 0))
  let c₅ :=
    Ledger.supply_acc_trans
      (Ledger.supply_acc_trans
        (Ledger.supply_acc_trans
          (Ledger.supply_acc_trans
            (Ledger.acc_xfer L₀ sender escrow P hs₀ he₀ hP) hacce)
          (Ledger.acc_xfer L₂ escrow sender R he₂ hs₂ hR₂))
        (Ledger.acc_xfer L₃ escrow coinbase T he₂ hc₂ hT₃))
      (Ledger.acc_burn L₄ escrow B he₂ hB₄)
  let hbτ : burned (τe ++ [Ev.burn escrow B]) = (0 + burned τe) + B :=
    Eq.trans (burned_append τe [Ev.burn escrow B])
      (congrArg (fun n => n + B) (Nat.zero_add (burned τe)).symm)
  let hmτ : minted (τe ++ [Ev.burn escrow B]) = 0 + minted τe :=
    Eq.trans (minted_append τe [Ev.burn escrow B])
      (Nat.zero_add (minted τe)).symm
  let hacc : L₅.supply + burned (τe ++ [Ev.burn escrow B])
      = L₀.supply + minted (τe ++ [Ev.burn escrow B]) :=
    Eq.trans (congrArg (fun n => L₅.supply + n) hbτ)
      (Eq.trans c₅ (congrArg (fun n => L₀.supply + n) hmτ.symm))
  let hconf : SiteConfined ([] : List A) [escrow] (τe ++ [Ev.burn escrow B]) :=
    SiteConfined.append hconfe (SiteConfined.burn ([] : List A) escrow B)
  ⟨L₅, τe ++ [Ev.burn escrow B],
   rfl, hacc,
   Eq.trans hbτ (congrArg (fun n => n + B) (Nat.zero_add (burned τe))),
   Eq.trans hmτ (Nat.zero_add (minted τe)),
   hconf,
   supply_le_of_confined_no_mint hacc hconf,
   ⟨e₅, rfl⟩⟩

audit_packet.guarantee: A settlement that debits P from the sender into an escrow and then pays out R to the sender, T to the coinbase and burns B from the escrow ends with: total supply plus cumulative burned equal to the initial supply plus cumulative minted (exact conservation), cumulative burned increased by exactly B, cumulative minted unchanged (and zero, since no mint site is authorized), final supply no greater than the initial supply, the escrow drained back to exactly its pre-settlement balance, and the live account set unchanged. Every deduction is guarded so that no subtraction can wrap or be silently truncated, which is what would otherwise inflate supply. Note the supply DROP equals the cumulative burn over the whole trace, burned(tau_e) + B, not B alone.
preconditions: escrow != sender (obligation hse): the escrow account is distinct from the payer
escrow != coinbase (obligation hec): the escrow account is distinct from the payout recipient
sender is a live/known account in the initial ledger L0 (obligation hs0)
escrow is a live/known account in the initial ledger L0 (obligation he0)
R + (T + B) = P (obligation hsplit): the three payout components sum EXACTLY to the amount P debited from the sender - no rounding, no leftover, no extra
P <= bal0(sender) (obligation hP): the sender can cover the full charge before any debit is performed
sender is live in the post-debit ledger L2 (obligation hs2)
escrow is live in the post-debit ledger L2 (obligation he2)
coinbase is live in the post-debit ledger L2 (obligation hc2) - the payout recipient must already exist in the accounted account set
bal2(escrow) = bal0(escrow) + P (obligation hesc): the escrow received exactly the full charge P, no more and no less

supply2 + burned(tau_e) = supply(L0 after debiting P from sender and crediting P to escrow) + minted(tau_e) (obligation hacce): the ledger reached by the debit phase is accounted-consistent with its event trace
SiteConfined [] [escrow] tau_e (obligation hconfe): in the trace so far, no event carries a mint site at all, and every burn site is the escrow

supporting_facts.claim: Exact global conservation is preserved across the whole settlement: final_supply + burned(tau) = initial_supply + minted(tau). Each intra-ledger transfer (sender->escrow of P, escrow->sender of R, escrow->coinbase of T) is supply-neutral, and the chain of accounted steps composes by transitivity.
supporting_facts.check: Sum every account balance before the settlement and after it. Compute delta_supply = supply_before - supply_after. Compare against (total burn amount recorded in the trace) - (total mint amount recorded in the trace).
supporting_facts.expected: supply_after + total_burned == supply_before + total_minted holds exactly, with each of the three transfers individually leaving total supply unchanged.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any transfer step changes the summed balances, or the equality holds only approximately / only modulo a word size, or the settlement is accounted with a net that differs from cumulative burn minus cumulative mint.

supporting_facts.claim: The burn step removes EXACTLY B from supply: burned(tau) = burned(tau_e) + B and the burn is accounted as supply_after + B = supply_before + 0. This equality depends on the guard B <= escrow_balance at the moment of the burn; the underlying accounting lemma only yields min(B, escrow_balance), so an unguarded burn would record a burn of B while destroying less than B.
supporting_facts.check: At the burn step, record the escrow balance before the burn, the burn amount B, and the escrow balance after. Verify balance_after = balance_before - B with no truncation, and that the burn event amount equals the supply reduction of that step.
supporting_facts.expected: escrow_balance_before >= B, escrow_balance_after == escrow_balance_before - B, and cumulative burned increases by exactly B.
supporting_facts.flag_if: B > escrow balance at the burn site; the balance clamps at zero or wraps; or the recorded burn amount (min(B, balance)) differs from the amount used in the accounting.

supporting_facts.claim: No new value is created anywhere in the settlement: minted(tau) = minted(tau_e), and confinement to an EMPTY mint-site list forces minted(tau) = 0. Every event in the extended trace has no mint site, and the only burn site is the escrow.
supporting_facts.check: Enumerate every balance-increasing effect produced by the settlement (escrow credit, payout to sender, payout to coinbase) and confirm each is matched by an equal decrement from another live account. Confirm no event in the trace is a mint, and every burn is attributed to the escrow account.
supporting_facts.expected: total minted over the whole settlement == 0; the trace's burn events all name the escrow as their source; the mint-site set is empty.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any credit lacks a matching debit; any event carries a mint site; a burn is attributed to an account other than the escrow; or a subtraction underflow manufactures a large balance that acts as an implicit mint.

supporting_facts.claim: Total supply is monotonically non-increasing across the settlement: final_supply <= initial_supply. Combined with the zero-mint fact this strengthens to final_supply + burned(tau) = initial_supply exactly, where burned(tau) is the CUMULATIVE burn of the whole trace (burned(tau_e) + B), not B alone.
supporting_facts.check: Compare the summed supply before and after settlement, and check the difference equals the cumulative burned recorded over the whole trace tau, not merely the final burn event.
supporting_facts.expected: final_supply <= initial_supply, and initial_supply - final_supply == burned(tau) == burned(tau_e) + B.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Supply after settlement exceeds supply before, or the drop differs from the cumulative recorded burn (in particular, an implementation that reconciles the drop against B alone while the trace burned more earlier).

supporting_facts.claim: Every one of the three escrow deductions is provably covered, in order, with an exact residual: the escrow holds e0 + (R + (T + B)) after being funded, so R <= escrow balance; after paying R it holds exactly e0 + (T + B), so T <= escrow balance; after paying T it holds exactly e0 + B, so B <= escrow balance; after the burn it holds exactly e0. Each residual is an EXACT equality, not merely a non-negativity claim.
supporting_facts.check: Instrument the escrow balance at four points: after funding, after the payout of R, after the payout of T, after the burn of B. Compare against e0+R+T+B, e0+T+B, e0+B, e0 respectively, where e0 is the escrow balance before the settlement.
supporting_facts.expected: The four observed balances match the four predicted values exactly, and each deduction amount is <= the balance immediately preceding it.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any observed escrow balance deviates from its predicted value; any deduction exceeds the current escrow balance; or the ordering of the three deductions is changed so that a later step is no longer covered.

supporting_facts.claim: A transfer of v from source s to a DISTINCT destination d leaves the source at exactly bal(s) - v, and writing one account's balance does not perturb any other account's balance. The distinctness side conditions (escrow != sender for the R payout, escrow != coinbase for the T payout) are load-bearing: without them the credit would overwrite the debit and the source residual would be wrong.
supporting_facts.check: For the escrow->sender payout of R and the escrow->coinbase payout of T, confirm the destination is not the escrow itself, and confirm that after each transfer the source balance is reduced by exactly the transferred amount while all uninvolved accounts are bit-identical.
supporting_facts.expected: source_after == source_before - v; destination_after == destination_before + v; all other balances unchanged; source != destination enforced.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A settlement where the sender or the coinbase equals the escrow account is processed without rejection or special handling; or a balance write clobbers a sibling account; or the source residual differs from bal - v.

supporting_facts.claim: The escrow is a pure conduit with zero residue: its final balance equals its pre-settlement balance exactly, bal_final(escrow) = bal_0(escrow).
supporting_facts.check: Compare the escrow balance before the settlement with its balance after settlement completes.
supporting_facts.expected: They are equal, for every settlement and for any starting escrow balance e0 including zero.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any dust, rounding remainder, or unpaid amount remains in (or is missing from) the escrow after settlement - that residue is an unaccounted claim on supply.

supporting_facts.claim: The set of live/accounted accounts after settlement equals the set after the debit phase: live_final = live_2. Settlement neither creates nor removes accounted accounts.
supporting_facts.check: Diff the live account set before and after the payout phase.
supporting_facts.expected: Identical sets, with no duplicates introduced.
supporting_facts.flag_if: An account is added, dropped, or duplicated during payout - a duplicate makes the same balance counted twice in the supply sum.

supporting_facts.claim: Trace accounting is additive and confinement is closed under extension: burned(t1 ++ t2) = burned(t1) + burned(t2), minted(t1 ++ t2) = minted(t1) + minted(t2), and appending a site-confined segment preserves site confinement. Appending the single burn event therefore adds exactly B to burned and 0 to minted.
supporting_facts.check: Verify that cumulative burn/mint counters are computed as a plain sum over all recorded events, and that appending this settlement's burn event to the prior trace preserves the mint-empty / burn-site-escrow confinement.
supporting_facts.expected: Counters are additive over trace concatenation; the extended trace is still confined to no mint sites and burn site = escrow.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Cumulative burn or mint is recomputed by overwrite rather than accumulation, events are dropped or reordered so a burn is lost or double-counted, or an appended event introduces an unconfined mint/burn site.

supporting_facts.claim: CRITICAL anti-underflow fact: without the coverage guard, a transfer of v from an account holding less than v does not fail - it raises total supply by exactly (v - bal(s)). The general accounting lemma is supply_after = supply_before + (v - bal(s)), which collapses to supply-neutral ONLY when v <= bal(s). Every guard here (P <= bal0(sender), and R, T, B each <= the escrow balance at their step) exists to force that subtraction to zero.
supporting_facts.check: Attempt settlement paths where the charge P exceeds the payer's balance and where a payout exceeds the escrow balance at its step (e.g. R, T or B derived from inflated inputs). Observe whether the deficit is rejected or silently absorbed.
supporting_facts.expected: Every such path is rejected before any balance is written; no path exists in which a debit is applied to an account with insufficient balance.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A saturating/clamping subtraction, a wrapping unsigned subtraction, or a debit applied without a preceding balance check - any of these creates (v - balance) out of nothing and is reachable by a single crafted input.

supporting_facts.claim: The supply sum is well-defined only over a DISTINCT account list, and updating one account's balance changes the sum by exactly (new - old) while leaving all non-matching entries untouched. Aliasing in the accounted account set breaks the conservation arithmetic itself.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm the accounted account collection contains no duplicate entries, and that a balance update to account a changes the supply total by exactly the delta on a and nothing else.
supporting_facts.expected: No duplicate accounts; supply delta after a single write == new_balance - old_balance.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The same account appears twice in the accounted set (e.g. sender == coinbase == escrow collapsing to one entry) without being deduplicated, or a write to one account perturbs the recorded total by a different amount.

derived_obligations.expected: The three payout components sum exactly to the amount debited from the sender.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The sum is computed with wrapping arithmetic, or the three components are derived independently such that their sum can differ from the charged amount.

derived_obligations.check: Assert P <= sender balance before the debit, and reject the settlement otherwise.
derived_obligations.expected: No debit is written unless the sender fully covers P.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The debit is written first and checked later, or the check uses a clamped/wrapped comparison.

derived_obligations.expected: Distinctness holds; otherwise the settlement path is rejected or handled by a separately verified path.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A settlement whose coinbase or sender coincides with the escrow is processed by the ordinary path.

derived_obligations.flag_if: Any deduction proceeds unchecked, or relies on the aggregate guard P <= sender balance instead of a per-step check.

derived_obligations.check: After settlement, assert escrow balance == its pre-settlement value, cumulative burned increased by exactly B, and cumulative minted unchanged (and zero under the empty mint-site confinement).
derived_obligations.expected: Zero escrow residue; burn delta == B; mint delta == 0.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Escrow retains or loses any amount, or the burn/mint deltas disagree with B/0.

derived_obligations.check: Recompute total supply after settlement and assert supply_after + cumulative_burned == supply_before + cumulative_minted and supply_after <= supply_before. Reconcile the supply drop against the CUMULATIVE burn of the trace, not against B alone.

derived_obligations.flag_if: Either relation fails for any settlement, including edge cases with zero R, zero T, zero B, a zero starting escrow balance, or a prior trace that already burned a nonzero amount.

audit_packet.derivation: The root theorem takes a ledger L0 in which the sender has been charged P and the escrow credited P (obligations hesc, hacce), with P split exactly as R + (T + B) (hsplit) and covered by the sender (hP), and all participants live and pairwise distinct where required (hs0, he0, hs2, he2, hc2, hse, hec), and the prior trace confined to no mint sites and burn site = escrow (hconfe). It then constructs the three payout steps in order: escrow -> sender of R, escrow -> coinbase of T, and a burn of B from the escrow. The escrow-guard and escrow-after lemmas (L001, L003, backed by L013/L015) give the exact residual after each step - e0+(T+B), then e0+B, then e0 - which both proves the coverage precondition for the NEXT step and pins the escrow's final balance to its initial value. The source-residual lemmas (L002/L014/L004/L016/L026) supply the exact bal - v semantics of a transfer and require the distinctness side conditions. The accounting lemmas (L006/L018 for transfers, L007/L020/L029 for the burn) are each supply-neutral or supply-exact ONLY under their coverage hypotheses; the general form (L027/L035) shows the failure mode explicitly - an uncovered debit of v raises supply by v - bal(s). Chaining the four accounted steps by transitivity (L005/L017) and rewriting the trace counters via the append laws (L008/L009) yields exact conservation, burned increased by exactly B, and minted unchanged; confinement is preserved by L010/L011, and confinement to an empty mint-site list forces minted = 0 (L033/L041/L050/L051/L053/L054/L055). That upgrades conservation to final_supply <= initial_supply (L012) and to final_supply + burned(tau) = initial_supply (L025/L032) - so the supply DROP is the cumulative burned(tau) = burned(tau_e) + B, while the DELTA contributed by this settlement's burn event is exactly B. The audit therefore checks the guards (OBS-1..OBS-5) that make every subtraction exact, and then the exact outcomes (OBS-6, OBS-7): escrow drained to its start balance, burn delta exactly B, nothing minted, supply reconciled against the cumulative burn.

theorem process_withdrawal_effect [DecidableEq A] (L : Ledger A) (w : A) (W : ℕ)
    (hw : w ∈ L.live) :
    (L.setBal w (L.bal w + W) hw).supply + burned [Ev.mint w W]
      = L.supply + minted [Ev.mint w W]
    ∧ SiteConfined [w] ([] : List A) [Ev.mint w W] :=
  ⟨Ledger.acc_setBal_add L w W hw, SiteConfined.mint ([] : List A) w W⟩

audit_packet.guarantee: For a point credit of amount W to an account w that is already a member of the live set, the state transition is exactly supply-conserving and site-confined: post-state total supply plus the burned total of the emitted trace equals pre-state total supply plus the minted total; the trace is the single event mint(w, W), so burned = 0 and minted = W and supply_post = supply_pre + W; every mint site in the trace is w and no event carries a burn site; and the write changes only w's balance, carrying the live set and its distinctness through unchanged.
preconditions: SCOPE (theorem hypothesis, not an implementation obligation): hw : w ∈ L.live. The guarantee is asserted only for executions in which the credited account is already enumerated in the live set that supply is summed over. Executions outside this scope are not covered by this item; do not read the hypothesis as a proved rejection or fail-closed behaviour.

MODEL INVARIANT (Ledger.live_distinct): the live account list is duplicate-free (EthTotal.Distinct L.live). Supply is defined as sumOver bal live, so the exactness of the delta depends on the target having exactly one entry in the enumeration. This is a condition on the state the checks are evaluated against.
MODEL INVARIANT (Ledger.bal_live): any account with non-zero balance is a member of live, so the enumeration used for supply covers all held balance.

The transition under check is exactly the point update L.setBal w (L.bal w + W) hw: the written value is the pre-state balance of w plus W, and only the bal component changes (setBalOfPoint carries live and live_distinct through unchanged).
The trace emitted for the transition is exactly the one-element list [Ev.mint w W]: one mint event, amount W, site w, no burn event.

MODELLING FIDELITY: amounts are ℕ in the proof (unbounded, no wraparound, no negatives). If the implementation's balance or supply arithmetic truncates, saturates, or wraps on bal w + W, the proved equality does not transfer.

supporting_facts.claim: Exact supply conservation, not a bound: (L.setBal w (L.bal w + W) hw).supply + burned [Ev.mint w W] = L.supply + minted [Ev.mint w W]; with burned [Ev.mint w W] = 0 and minted [Ev.mint w W] = W, post-state total supply equals pre-state total supply plus exactly W.
supporting_facts.check: Around one such credit, compute total issued supply as the sum of balances over the whole live set immediately before and immediately after, alongside the amount W applied and the amount recorded as issued. Compare supply_post - supply_pre against W for exact equality, for W = 0, W = 1, a typical amount, and the largest representable amount.
supporting_facts.expected: supply_post - supply_pre == W exactly, for every W including W = 0; the issued/minted accounting for the operation equals W and the burned accounting equals 0.
supporting_facts.flag_if: supply_post - supply_pre differs from W in either direction (credit applied twice, applied to both the account and a mirror/aggregate counter, supply recomputed from a stale snapshot, W rounded or unit-converted, or wrap/saturation at the representable maximum). Any inequality is a break in the issuance accounting.

supporting_facts.claim: The point write REPLACES the target's contribution to supply rather than adding to it: (L.setBal a v ha).supply + L.bal a = L.supply + v. The proved +W delta holds only because the written value is the pre-state balance plus W; writing an absolute v computed from anything else makes the supply delta v - bal w.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm the value written is derived from the account's current, freshly-read balance plus W, and that the supply figure is derived from the same account set the write lands in. Exercise a target with a non-zero pre-state balance, and a case where the balance is read before another adjustment to the same account in the same operation.
supporting_facts.expected: written_balance == balance_read_immediately_before + W, and the resulting supply delta v - bal_pre(w) == W.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The written balance is an absolute value not anchored to the current balance, is computed from a stale or cached read of bal w, or the operation both adds W to the account and separately adds W to an aggregate supply figure. Each field still looks plausible while the delta is not W.

supporting_facts.claim: The delta is exact only under the distinctness hypothesis: sumOver (update f a v) l + f a = sumOver f l + v requires a ∈ l and Distinct l. Duplicate entries for the target in the enumerated set break the equality.
supporting_facts.check: Verify that the live set enumerated for supply accounting is duplicate-free and that the target resolves to exactly one entry in it, under the same equality relation the write uses to locate the target. Evaluate a state in which the target identity appears more than once in the enumeration and observe the supply delta.
supporting_facts.expected: The enumeration carries no duplicate entries under the same equality relation the write uses; exactly one entry is updated; supply delta remains W.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Duplicate or aliasing entries are representable in the enumerated set, or the equality relation used to locate the target differs from the one under which distinctness is maintained (e.g. one path normalises the identifier and the other does not). Then one credit multiplies its amount across duplicates.

supporting_facts.claim: No collateral mutation: updating an account not present in a list leaves that list's sum unchanged (sumOver (update f a v) l = sumOver f l when a ∉ l). With the point update, only the target's balance contributes to the change.
supporting_facts.check: Diff the full pre- and post-state account map for one credit: enumerate every account whose balance changed and every change to the membership of the live set itself.
supporting_facts.expected: Exactly one balance changed, that of w, by exactly +W; the live set membership is identical before and after (setBalOfPoint carries live and live_distinct through unchanged).
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any account other than w has a changed balance, or the live set gains, loses, or reorders entries as a side effect of the credit. Collateral writes to a neighbouring entry (index/offset error, shared slot, iteration reuse) redistribute balance while the target's own balance still reads correctly.

supporting_facts.claim: Mint-site confinement: SiteConfined [w] [] [Ev.mint w W] — every event in the trace whose mintSite is Some d has d = w. The operation may credit at exactly one site, the account the balance write targets.
supporting_facts.check: Collect every issuance/mint event the operation emits and compare each event's site against the account identity the balance write lands on and the identity the membership condition was evaluated for.
supporting_facts.expected: Every mint event emitted names w — the same account the write targets — as its site, and there is exactly one such event, carrying amount W.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A mint is emitted whose site is any account other than the one written, more than one mint is emitted for the operation, or the identity used to write the balance and the identity recorded in the issuance event can diverge (independent re-derivation, re-parse, or re-normalisation between the two uses).

supporting_facts.claim: Burn-site emptiness: the burn site set is [], so no event in the trace may have a burnSite of Some s, and burned [Ev.mint w W] = 0. The accounting equality relies on the burn total being exactly zero, not merely small.
supporting_facts.check: Assert the credit path emits zero burn events and contributes zero to any burned/destroyed accumulator, including on every early-exit, retry, or error branch.
supporting_facts.expected: burned contribution of the operation == 0 and no emitted event carries a burn site.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The path records any burn, debit, or destroyed amount — even a compensating one intended to balance the books. A non-zero burn paired with the +W mint keeps the aggregate equality looking correct while destroying balance held by whichever account is debited.

supporting_facts.claim: Scope, not behaviour: the whole result is conditioned on hw : w ∈ L.live. The theorem establishes neither the supply equality nor the confinement for a credit to an account outside the live set, and it does not establish any particular handling of that case.
supporting_facts.check: When evaluating FACT-1 through FACT-6, confirm the credited account is a member of the same enumerated live set that supply is summed over — i.e. that the observed execution is inside the theorem's scope. Record executions where it is not as out of scope for this item rather than as pass or fail.
supporting_facts.expected: Every execution used as evidence for the checks above has the credited account already enumerated in the account set supply is computed from, and membership is evaluated against that same set rather than a separate one.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The membership condition is evaluated against a different set than the one supply is summed over, so an execution can appear in scope while the credited balance sits outside the enumeration used for supply. In that case the checks above are being evaluated against a state the theorem does not cover.

derived_obligations.check: For each route into the balance write (fast path, batch path, replay/reprocessing path), determine whether the account credited on that route is a member of the enumerated live set at the moment of the write, so that the route's coverage by this item is explicit.
derived_obligations.expected: Each route is classified as in scope (target already enumerated in the live set supply is summed over) or out of scope; in-scope routes satisfy FACT-1 through FACT-6.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A route's scope cannot be determined, or membership on that route is evaluated against a set other than the one supply is computed from.

derived_obligations.check: Establish that the enumerated live set is duplicate-free under exactly the equality relation the credit path uses to locate the target, and that the target resolves to exactly one entry.
derived_obligations.expected: No duplicate entries under that relation; the delta checks in FACT-1 and FACT-3 are evaluated on such a state.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Duplicates are representable in the enumeration, or two identifiers the credit path treats as equal are treated as distinct by the enumeration used for supply (or vice versa).

derived_obligations.check: Run a differential invariant test around the operation: recompute total supply by summing all live balances before and after, and compare the delta to the sum of amounts in the mint events emitted minus the sum of amounts in any burn events emitted.
derived_obligations.expected: recomputed_supply_post + total_burned == recomputed_supply_pre + total_minted, holding exactly, with total_burned == 0.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The recomputed identity fails, or supply is only ever read from a cached aggregate never cross-checked against the recomputed sum — a drifting aggregate hides every failure above.

derived_obligations.check: Fuzz W and the pre-state balance of w across the full representable range, including 0, 1, the maximum representable balance, and values whose sum exceeds the representable maximum of the balance and of the supply accumulator.
derived_obligations.expected: The +W delta holds exactly for all in-range values; any value that cannot be represented is rejected explicitly rather than wrapping, saturating, or truncating.
derived_obligations.flag_if: bal w + W wraps, saturates, or truncates, or the supply accumulator overflows while individual balances do not. The proof is over ℕ and offers no protection here; a wrap turns a large credit into an arbitrary supply change.

derived_obligations.check: Snapshot the complete account state (all balances plus live-set membership and ordering) before and after one credit and assert the diff has exactly one entry.
derived_obligations.expected: The diff contains exactly the pair (w, +W); membership and the enumerated set itself are unchanged.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The diff contains any additional entry, or the live set changes as a side effect of the credit.

derived_obligations.check: Verify that the account identity used to write the balance is the same value, from the same read, as the identity recorded in the emitted mint event and the identity the membership condition was evaluated for — no independent re-derivation, re-parse, or re-normalisation between the three uses.
derived_obligations.expected: A single account value flows to the membership evaluation, the balance write, and the event site.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The identity is re-derived independently for any of the three uses, allowing the account in scope, the account credited, and the account accounted for to diverge.

audit_packet.derivation: The root theorem is a conjunction. Its first component is the accounting equality from L001 (Ledger.acc_setBal_add), which specialises L003 (supply_setBal_add: (setBal d (bal d + v)).supply = supply + v) to a zero burn total. L003 rests on L008 (supply_setBal: the write replaces the target's contribution) cancelled by L007/L010 to isolate the delta, and L008 rests on L011/L014 (sumOver_update), exact only under a ∈ l and Distinct l. L015 supplies the complementary case — an update outside the list changes nothing — which pins the effect to the single target (FACT-4). The second component is L002 (SiteConfined.mint), assembled from L005 (site_singleton) and L006 (no_site, making the burn-site obligation vacuous), quantified by L004/L009. The hypothesis hw : w ∈ L.live and the structure field live_distinct are carried as SCOPE and MODEL INVARIANT preconditions, and FACT-7/OBS-1/OBS-2 test only that the checks are evaluated against a state satisfying them and against the same enumeration supply is summed over; they do not assert any rejection, fail-closed, or duplicate-refusal behaviour, since the theorem proves none. The packet preserves the equality form (supply_post = supply_pre + W) rather than a monotonicity or success flag, the exact burn total of 0 rather than 'few burns', and the membership conclusions of L005/L006 as site-identity checks rather than an unspecific event check.

omitted_facts.reason: EthTotal.forall_mem_singleton is quantifier plumbing discharging a ∀-over-a-singleton-list goal. Its security content is carried by FACT-5, which states the confinement conclusion it helps establish.
EthTotal.add_right_cancel is a ℕ cancellation step used to isolate the supply delta from L008. It introduces no state, event, or membership condition an implementation could violate independently.

EthTotal.eqOfMemSingleton (membership in a singleton implies equality) is list plumbing supporting L004/L005; its audit-relevant consequence — the mint site equals the written account — is stated directly in FACT-5.
EthTotal.add_left_cancel is a ℕ cancellation lemma with no implementation-facing condition; the arithmetic exactness it supports is checked end-to-end by FACT-1 and OBS-4.
EthTotal.memConsElim is the cons-case eliminator for list membership, used to structure the induction in L009/L014. It is a proof-structuring device, not a state condition.

EthTotal.notMemNil closes the base case of the same inductions. Its only audit-visible consequence — an account absent from the enumerated set has no entry contributing to the sum — is covered by FACT-4 and FACT-7.
