audit_packet.guarantee: For a transfer of value v from s to d, both members of the live account list of a ledger whose total supply is the sum of balances over that list, if the debit is computed with truncated (saturating) subtraction bal(s)-v and the credit with the full v, then whenever bal(s) < v the resulting total supply is strictly greater than the pre-transfer total supply, by exactly v - bal(s). The implementation must make this state unreachable: reject v > bal(s) before any balance write, so every applied transfer conserves total supply exactly.
preconditions: ROOT obligation hs: s is a member of the live account list (caller/model precondition, not itself an implementation check)
ROOT obligation hd: d is a member of the live account list (caller/model precondition)
ROOT obligation hgt: bal(s) < v — the guarded overdraft state the theorem reasons about
Model structure: the live list is duplicate-free (Ledger.live_distinct) and any account with nonzero balance is live (Ledger.bal_live)
Balances are naturals with truncated subtraction: x - y saturates at 0 when y >= x rather than going negative or erroring. The model imposes no upper bound on balances.

supporting_facts.claim: Root theorem: with s and d live and bal(s) < v, the truncated-debit-then-full-credit sequence yields a ledger whose total supply is strictly greater than before — supply is created out of nothing.
supporting_facts.check: Construct a state with two live accounts, set bal(s)=k, and attempt a transfer of value v > k from s to d. Sum all balances before and after.
supporting_facts.expected: The transfer is rejected by the balance check and no balance is written; the summed total is unchanged.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The transfer is applied (s clamped to 0, d credited v) and the summed total after is strictly greater than before.

supporting_facts.claim: Exact quantification, not merely an inequality: the post-transfer supply equals supply + (v - bal(s)). The amount created is exactly the shortfall, determined by the chosen v.
supporting_facts.check: For several (bal(s), v) pairs with v > bal(s), record post_supply - pre_supply if the transfer is (incorrectly) applied.
supporting_facts.expected: No transfer with v > bal(s) is ever applied, so the difference is never observable; when v <= bal(s) the difference is exactly 0.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any applied transfer yields post_supply - pre_supply == v - bal(s) > 0, or any nonzero difference at all — a weaker check that only asserts 'supply did not decrease' would miss the exact-equality break.

supporting_facts.claim: General conservation law for the debit-then-credit pair: post_supply + min(v, bal(s)) = pre_supply + v. Supply is conserved exactly when the debited amount min(v, bal(s)) equals the credited amount v.
supporting_facts.check: Instrument the transfer path to record the amount actually removed from s and the amount actually added to d, then compare them for each executed transfer.
supporting_facts.expected: debited == credited == v for every executed transfer, so post_supply = pre_supply.
supporting_facts.flag_if: debited < credited for any executed transfer (i.e. debited == min(v, bal(s)) < v).

supporting_facts.claim: The credit leg is exact and unconditional: setting bal(d) := bal(d) + v for live d raises total supply by exactly v, with no clamping or cap on the recipient side.
supporting_facts.check: Apply only the recipient-side credit and measure the change in total supply.
supporting_facts.expected: Total supply rises by exactly v on the credit leg — so the debit leg must remove exactly v to restore the total.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The credit leg can be applied without a matching, equally sized debit leg having already succeeded, or the two legs are not atomic under any failure path.

supporting_facts.claim: The debit leg is deficient under truncation: supply_after_debit + min(v, bal(s)) = pre_supply, i.e. the debit removes only min(v, bal(s)), strictly less than v exactly when bal(s) < v.
supporting_facts.check: Apply only the sender-side debit with v > bal(s) and measure the removal from total supply.
supporting_facts.expected: The debit is refused before mutation because v > bal(s); no partial debit state exists.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The debit clamps bal(s) to 0 and removes only bal(s), leaving the shortfall v - bal(s) uncovered — especially if the credit leg then proceeds.

supporting_facts.claim: Single-account update accounting: for a live account a in a duplicate-free list, supply(setBal a v) + bal(a) = supply + v. The total tracks per-account writes exactly only when the list has no duplicate entries and the written account is a member.
supporting_facts.check: Verify the account/balance container admits no duplicate keys for the same account and that every balance write targets an account already present in (or correctly inserted into) that container.
supporting_facts.expected: Each write changes the total by exactly (new_value - old_value); no duplicate key can be updated on one path and summed on another.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Duplicate or aliased account entries exist, or a balance write targets an account not accounted for in the supply sum.

supporting_facts.claim: Truncated-subtraction identity: min(v, b) + (b - v) = b for naturals, with b - v = 0 whenever b <= v and min(v, b) = b in that same case. Truncated subtraction silently loses exactly v - b of value instead of failing.
supporting_facts.check: Locate every truncating/saturating subtraction on a balance in the transfer path and confirm each is guarded by a prior check that the minuend is at least the subtrahend.
supporting_facts.expected: Every balance subtraction is preceded by an explicit check bal >= v that aborts the whole transfer on failure; the subtraction can therefore never truncate.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any balance subtraction can execute with subtrahend > minuend and silently produce 0 (or a clamped value) instead of aborting the transfer.

supporting_facts.claim: Strict positivity of the shortfall: bal(s) < v implies 0 < v - bal(s). The increase is never zero in the overdraft case — every overdraft transfer creates a strictly positive amount.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm there is no boundary case in which an overdraft (v > bal(s)) is treated as harmless or as a no-op.
supporting_facts.expected: Overdraft is always an error path; there is no v > bal(s) that is silently tolerated.
supporting_facts.flag_if: An overdraft is tolerated on the assumption that the discrepancy is zero or negligible — for v = bal(s) + 1 it is already a strictly positive unbacked increase.

supporting_facts.claim: Updating an account that is not a member of the summed list leaves the sum unchanged — a write to a non-tracked account creates a balance the supply accounting never sees.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm sender and recipient are resolved into the same account set used to compute the total before either leg is applied, including newly created recipients.
supporting_facts.expected: Both s and d are members of the accounted set at the time of the write, so every credit is visible to supply accounting.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A credit can land on an account outside the accounted set (e.g. an untracked or lazily created recipient), making the credited value invisible to any conservation check.

supporting_facts.claim: Order bounds on the actual debit: min(v, bal(s)) <= v and min(v, bal(s)) <= bal(s), and min is symmetric — the debit is capped by the sender's available balance and can never reach v when bal(s) < v.
supporting_facts.check: Assert the recorded debit amount satisfies debit <= bal(s) and debit == v for every executed transfer.
supporting_facts.expected: Both hold simultaneously, which forces v <= bal(s) — exactly the balance-check precondition.
supporting_facts.flag_if: debit <= bal(s) holds while debit == v fails, i.e. the cap binds and the transfer still proceeds.

derived_obligations.check: In the value-transfer path, confirm the sender-balance check (bal(s) >= v) executes before any balance mutation and aborts the entire transfer, not just the debit leg, when it fails.
derived_obligations.expected: Insufficient balance aborts the transfer atomically with no balance written to either s or d.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The check is missing, occurs after a mutation, is advisory only, or aborts the debit while allowing the credit to persist.

derived_obligations.check: Replace or guard every truncating/saturating balance subtraction on the transfer path so an underflow is an explicit error rather than a clamp to zero.
derived_obligations.expected: Truncation is unreachable on the transfer path: either the operation errors, or an explicit prior check makes truncation impossible.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any subtraction on a balance can clamp at zero without raising an error.

derived_obligations.check: Assert a conservation invariant over the whole accounted set: the sum of all balances before a transfer equals the sum after, as a test property and, if feasible, a debug-mode assertion on the transfer path.
derived_obligations.expected: The total is exactly identical before and after every applied transfer, including v = 0, v = bal(s), and v = bal(s) + 1.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any applied transfer changes the summed total in either direction; an increase matches the theorem's inflation case, a decrease indicates silent value loss.

derived_obligations.check: Property-test the transfer over the overdraft region: v = bal(s) + 1, v much larger than bal(s), and v exceeding the current total of all balances.
derived_obligations.expected: Every such transfer is rejected; the total and both account balances are unchanged.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any such input is accepted and the total increases by v - bal(s).

derived_obligations.check: Verify the account container satisfies the structural assumptions the accounting rests on: no duplicate/aliased entries per account, and both sender and recipient present in the accounted set before any write.
derived_obligations.expected: Distinctness and membership hold at every transfer, so per-account writes map one-to-one onto changes in the total.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Duplicate/aliased entries are possible, or a balance write targets an account outside the accounted set.

audit_packet.derivation: The root theorem (FACT-1) gives a strict increase in total supply under three obligations: s live, d live, bal(s) < v. FACT-2 sharpens the inequality to the exact identity post_supply = pre_supply + (v - bal(s)), so the created amount is exactly the shortfall — a check that only asserts non-decrease would be strictly weaker than the lemma. That identity comes from FACT-3's conservation law post_supply + min(v, bal(s)) = pre_supply + v, which decomposes into the exact credit leg (FACT-4: +v, unconditional) and the deficient debit leg (FACT-5: only min(v, bal(s)) removed). Both legs reduce to the single-account accounting rule (FACT-6), valid only because the live list is duplicate-free and the written account is a member — hence membership and distinctness are genuine assumptions of the model, checked in OBS-5 as a model/implementation correspondence rather than as an independent implementation invariant. FACT-7 gives the mechanism: truncated subtraction satisfies min(v,b) + (b - v) = b, so it silently absorbs exactly the shortfall instead of failing; FACT-10's min bounds show the debit is capped at bal(s) and cannot reach v in the overdraft case; FACT-8 shows the shortfall is strictly positive, so no overdraft is benign. FACT-9 closes the flank where a credit lands outside the accounted set and escapes conservation checks. The implementation guard is the contrapositive: enforce bal(s) >= v atomically before any write (OBS-1), make truncation unreachable (OBS-2), and assert exact conservation (OBS-3) over the overdraft region (OBS-4) with a well-formed account set (OBS-5).

omitted_facts.reason: add_right_cancel is a natural-number cancellation step used to rearrange the supply equations; it carries no independent security content beyond the equalities exposed as FACT-2/FACT-3/FACT-5.
add_left_cancel is the mirror cancellation lemma backing L005; proof plumbing with no implementation-checkable consequence.
notMemNil states nothing is a member of the empty list — a base case of the list induction behind sumOver_update, adding no check beyond the membership preconditions already listed.
memConsElim is the cons-case eliminator driving the same list induction; structural recursion machinery whose security-relevant outcome is captured by FACT-6 and FACT-9.
